newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi clarifies auditor's Italy pensions comment.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi clarifies auditor's Italy pensions comment.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Friday that comments on pensions by state auditor Andrea Monorchio did not reflect the government's position on the matter.

Monorchio told a parliamentary commission on Thursday that so-called seniority pensions, which can be drawn after 40 years of contributions have been paid by an employee into a state retirement fund, should be phased out.
He said in future all Italians should expect to retire at the age of 65 and earlier pensions should be granted only in special cases.
Ciampi, asked by reporters whether the Treasury and government shared Monorchio's views, replied:

"(The proposal) is not from the Treasury or the government...there is only one valid line and it is that declared by the Prime Minister...who has announced that he is beginning talks with unions and employers."

The Italian cabinet has approved a package for 15.5 trillion lire of additional budget-deficit cutting measures this year which has drawn criticism from industry and opposition alike for not addressing structural reforms to state spending.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said eventual reform will be enshrined in the 1998 budget. Unions have constantly said that the pensions system cannot be touched before 1998, as agreed in a previous pension reform deal worked out in 1995.
